Vide this common judgment, I shall decide the instant four claim petitions filed separately under S e c t i o n 1 6 6 o f t h e M o t o r V e h i c l e A c t ,

The separate DARs (Detailed Accident Report) already filed by the Investigating Agency in the present matters have also been clubbed/ attached with the respective claim petitions.
2. In connection with the accident, FIR no.26/2019, under sections 279/337/304-A IPC, was registered at PS Anand Vihar on the statement of injured Imran (petitioner in DAR-MACT no.369/2019).

As per FIR/ DARs, on the aforesaid date and time, the injured Imran, driver by profession, in his Eeco car bearing no. DL1RT-3230, was taking the hardware goods of his friend Shamshad (deceased in MACT no. 368/2019) to Anand Vihar.
In this car, Abdul Wahab (deceased in MACT no.175/2019) was sitting on the seat next to Imran (driver) and deceased Shamshad was sitting behind Imran.

At the aforesaid time, when their car was climbing the Anand Vihar Flyover towards Anand Vihar Bus Stop, ahead of Ramprastha Red Light Signal, a Ford Eeco Sport car bearing no. DL10-CT-5595 (hereinafter, 'offending vehicle') being driven by respondent no.1 Akshay Jain at a high speed was seen coming from the front (on the road going from Anand Vihar Bus Stop to Dilshad Garden) and it jumped over the divider and fell on the Eeco Car being driven by ____________________________________________________________ Imran.
As a result of the accident, Imran received injuries, whereas other two occupants of Eeco car, namely Shamshad and Abdul Wahab, died on the spot.

One of the occupants of the offending vehicle,
namely Garv Sehgal (deceased in MACT no.200/2019) also died as a result of the accident.
Another occupant of offending vehicle, namely Akshay Jain (driver), suffered injuries.
3. Immediately after the accident, all the injured/ deceased were taken to hospital.

As per MLCs prepared at LBS Hospital, Shamshad and Abdul Wahab were declared brought dead, whereas nature of injury of Imran and that of respondent no.1 Akshay Jain were stated to be under observation.
Further, vide MLC prepared at Dr. Hedgewar Hospital, Garv Sehgal was also declared brought dead.

4. During investigation, it was found out that at the time of the accident, the offending vehicle was being driven by respondent no.1 Akshay Jain, owned by respondent no.2 Mohan Jain and insured with respondent no.3/ Tata AIG General Insurance Co. Ltd.

14. Issue no.1, being interlinked in all the cases, shall be decided here together by my common findings.
15. It is the settled proposition of law that, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
A holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.

15. It is the settled proposition of law that, in an action founded on the principle of fault liability, the proof of rash and negligent driving of the offending vehicle is sine qua non.
However, the standard of proof is not as strict as applied in criminal cases and evidence is to be tested on the touchstone of the preponderance of probabilities.
A holistic view is to be taken while dealing with the Claim Petition based upon negligence.
Strict rules of evidence are not applicable in an inquiry conducted by the Claims Tribunal.
Reference may be made to the judgments titled as New India Assurance Co.
Ltd. v. Sakshi Bhutani & Others., MAC APP. No. 550/2011 decided on 02.07.2012, Bimla Devi &
